name: Virginia Art Factory
blurb: Downtown arts nonprofit with a gallery, community theater productions, visual art and dance classes, and a summer concert series. Programs for ages five and up.

name: Nova Labs
blurb: Makerspace with shops for woodworking, metalworking, stained glass, sewing, jewelry and leather. Book a single class, or join as a member for ongoing access to the tools.

name: Girls Who Hike Virginia
blurb: Free or low-cost group hikes for women+, led by volunteer guides and rated by difficulty so beginners can start easy. Most coordination happens in their Facebook group.

name: Turning The Tables
blurb: Grassroots Indivisible group holding postcard-writing parties to reach voters, voter registration drives, and civics and media-literacy workshops.

name: Visibility Brigade
blurb: Volunteers who hold banners and signs on highway overpasses at rush hour.

name: Reflex Improv
blurb: Six-week improv classes from total beginner up to performance level, plus musical improv. No acting experience needed; intro courses run $230 to $275.

name: Craftspace
blurb: A stocked craft studio you can use by the hour, with Cricut machines, heat presses and laser cutters, plus classes, an adult craft night, and kids' camps.

name: Dabble CRC
blurb: Arts-and-crafts thrift store selling secondhand yarn, fabric, paint and scrapbooking supplies cheaply, with classes for kids, teens and adults.

name: Romp n’Roll
blurb: Play gym for kids from 3 months to 5 years, with parent-and-child classes in gym, music, art, cooking and dance, plus open play and camps. A good way to meet other parents of little ones; membership-based, with a paid trial class.

name: Pozez JCC of Northern Virginia
blurb: Pool, gym and group fitness classes, daily open-play pickleball, adult classes and affinity groups, and volunteer roles like driving seniors to appointments. Rooted in Jewish community life; most facilities run on membership, and guests can play pickleball on a day pass.

name: BreadBreakers Reston
blurb: Hosted dinners for people from different backgrounds and beliefs, where the goal is understanding each other rather than debating. Meets at Lake Anne Community Center or local restaurants; run by a church but open to everyone.
